title: Global problems
subtitle: hurricane, flood, pollution, war
summary: Name the big problems in the world - natural disasters like floods and earthquakes, and man-made problems like pollution, war and traffic jams.

lesson.heading: Natural disasters
lesson.text: Some problems come from nature. A **hurricane** is a very strong wind. A **snowstorm** is a lot of snow and wind at the same time. A **forest fire** happens when it is very dry and the trees catch fire.

examples.text: There was a **hurricane** there last year. It broke a lot of windows.
Siberia often has **snowstorms** in the winter.
It was very dry in August and there was a big **forest fire**.

lesson.heading: Nature words and what they mean
rows: a lot of snow and wind at the same time
when it is very dry and trees catch fire
lesson.note: Flood is also a verb: the river often floods after heavy rain.

lesson.heading: Earthquakes and floods
lesson.text: An **earthquake** happens when the earth moves. A **flood** happens when there is too much water and it goes over the river banks.

examples.text: San Francisco has had a lot of **earthquakes**.
There were serious **floods** in the north yesterday.
The river often **floods** after heavy rain.

lesson.heading: Too many people
lesson.text: There are too many people in some places, and the cities are too **crowded**. Many people are **poor** (they do not have enough money), **hungry** (they do not have enough food), **homeless** (they do not have a place to live) or **unemployed** (they do not have a job).

examples.text: The city centre is very **crowded** on Saturday afternoon.
When people are **homeless**, they sometimes sleep on the streets.
He lost his job last year and he is still **unemployed**.

lesson.heading: Pollution
lesson.text: **Pollution** is when the air, the water or the earth is dirty and bad for people, plants and animals. A river or a city can be **polluted**.

examples.text: Cars make air **pollution** worse in towns.
The river is **polluted** and a lot of fish have died.
The water is so **polluted** that people cannot drink it.

lesson.heading: War and strikes
lesson.text: A **war** is fighting between two or more countries or nationalities. A **strike** is when people refuse to work because, for example, they want more money. We say people are *on strike*.

examples.text: The American **War** of Independence started in 1775 and ended in 1783. It lasted for eight years.
The teachers are **on strike** today, so the school is closed.
Their wages were very low, so the workers went **on strike**.

lesson.heading: Problems on the roads
lesson.text: A **car crash** is when two cars hit one another. A **traffic jam** is when there are so many cars on the road that they cannot easily move. The **rush hour** is the time of day when everyone is going to work or coming home.

examples.text: He had a **car crash** on the way to work.
The **traffic jams** in the city are terrible in the **rush hour**.
I hate driving in the city in the **rush hour**.

lesson.text: Try to listen to or watch the news in English every day and write down new words about world problems.

exercises.prompt: A very strong wind is a ___.
exercises.explanation: A hurricane is a very strong wind.

exercises.prompt: The buildings shook and the ground moved. There was an ___.
exercises.explanation: An earthquake is when the earth moves.

exercises.prompt: Match the word on the left with the word on the right to make a phrase from this unit.
There was too much water in the north yesterday and the houses were under water. What were there?
exercises.explanation: A flood is too much water; the water goes over the river banks.

exercises.prompt: Cars make air ___ worse in towns.
exercises.explanation: Pollution is when the air, water or earth is dirty and bad for us.

exercises.statement: People who do not have a job are unemployed.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Unemployed means you do not have a job.

exercises.prompt: Their wages were very low, so the workers went on ___.
exercises.explanation: A strike is when people refuse to work, for example because they want more money.

exercises.prompt: Which problems come from nature and which ones do people make?
When people are ___, they sometimes sleep on the streets.
exercises.explanation: Homeless people do not have a place to live.

exercises.statement: When it is very dry and the trees catch fire, we call it a snowstorm.
exercises.explanation: When it is very dry and the trees catch fire, we call it a forest fire.

exercises.prompt: There are so many cars on the road that they cannot easily move. What is this?
exercises.explanation: A traffic jam is when the cars on the road cannot move easily.

exercises.prompt: I hate driving in the city in the ___, when everyone is going to work.
exercises.explanation: The rush hour is the time of day when there is most traffic.

exercises.prompt: Say what happened in the south last year.
exercises.answer: There was a hurricane in the south last year.
exercises.explanation: We say there was a hurricane / a flood / an earthquake.
